object_description: linear clinic complex on a raised parking plateau
design_condition: The raised plateau creates a self-contained complex directly connected to the main street, but it does not sufficiently engage with the surrounding landscape or form an understandable overall system with the existing buildings.

positive.statement: A unique, coherent world is created on the mineral belvedere.

position.rationale: Raised, orthogonal footprint and low horizontal elevations indicate a coherent plateau-based site.

positive.statement: The architectural expression and materialization are coherent and create a homely atmosphere.

position.rationale: Long, consistent building edges and repeated elevation bands provide a façade-level expression anchor.

positive.statement: The development concept is operationally sound, with the school and sports hall as independent functional units.

position.rationale: The elongated top footprint and separated massing suggest multiple independent functional units.

negative.statement: The project is more related to the object itself and less concerned with the location.

position.rationale: The compact linear complex is clearly bounded, supporting a whole-building location for the object-focused criticism.

negative.statement: What is missing is a committed engagement with the landscape and a coherent transition into the large landscape area.

position.target: transition into the large landscape area
position.rationale: The outer north-east building edge provides the most plausible sampled boundary toward surrounding landscape.

negative.statement: The limited open space between the clinic and the street is not enough.

position.target: open space between the clinic and the street
position.rationale: A narrow strip along the south/front edge represents the constrained street-facing open-space zone.

negative.statement: The open spaces created in the building are trapped and do not seem suitable for an appropriate stay.

position.target: open spaces created in the building
position.rationale: The central portion of the elongated footprint is the most plausible location for enclosed internal open spaces.

negative.statement: The direct connection to the street leaves it little breathing space as an access road to the district.

position.rationale: The south/front perimeter directly meets the represented building edge and is the likely street access interface.

negative.statement: The transition from the assigned outdoor spaces to the landscape area is difficult.

position.target: transition from assigned outdoor spaces to landscape
position.rationale: The eastern outer edge offers a plausible sampled location for difficult outdoor-to-landscape transitions.

negative.statement: The middle access corridor leaves little scope to create a homely ambience.

position.rationale: The middle of the linear plan is the best constrained anchor for an internal access corridor.

negative.statement: The architectural expression and spatial atmosphere appear questionable for a child and adolescent psychiatric clinic.

position.rationale: The broad criticism concerns the low-rise building mass and its repeated, schematic exterior bands.

negative.statement: The facade expression is hard in the context of child and adolescent psychiatry.

position.rationale: A longitudinal side façade is visible across the elevations and provides a representative expression anchor.

negative.statement: The patient-room windows provide little intimacy near the street.

position.rationale: The south/front façade at upper wall level is the constrained location nearest the street.

negative.statement: The internal vertical circulation system is complicated and not very user-friendly.

position.rationale: Internal circulation is not distinguishable, so the central building surface provides a constrained approximation.

negative.statement: The design expression remains strict and schematic, lacking subtlety and playfulness.

position.rationale: The broad judgment is anchored to a representative portion of the strict, orthogonal building envelope.
